title: The chess player in the park
summary: A boy who has just moved to a new city learns chess from an old man who plays alone every afternoon.
paragraphs: When Samir's family moved to the city, he didn't know anyone. School was big and noisy, and the other boys had been friends since they were small. In the afternoons he walked home slowly through the park, because he didn't want to arrive at the empty flat, where his parents would not be home until seven.

In the middle of the park there were stone tables with chessboards painted on them. Every afternoon, an old man sat at one of them, playing against himself. He moved a white piece, thought for a long time, then turned the board and moved a black one. One day, Samir stopped to watch. The man didn't look up. "Do you play?" he asked. "No," said Samir. The man pushed the black pieces towards him. "Then today you start."

His name was Mr Abramov. He had been an engineer, and he explained chess like a machine: every piece had a job, and the {{trick}} was to make them work together. He was a strict teacher. If Samir moved without thinking, he said, "Why?" and waited until Samir had a real answer. Samir lost every game for two months.

But he started to think differently. At school, in maths, he looked at problems the way he looked at the board: what is the goal, what can each piece do, what will happen next? His marks improved. One day, two boys from his class saw him playing in the park and asked if they could watch. The next week, they asked him to teach them.

By spring there were six people around Mr Abramov's table every afternoon: Samir, his classmates, a girl from the flats nearby and a {{retired}} bus driver who had played as a young man. Mr Abramov pretended to be annoyed by the noise, but he brought extra chess sets from home. In June, Samir finally won a game against him. Mr Abramov looked at the board for a long time. Then he stood up and shook Samir's hand, very {{formally}}. "Now," he said, "you are ready to lose to better players."

trick.meaning: a clever way of doing something

retired.meaning: no longer working, usually because of age

formally.meaning: in a serious, correct and official way

questions.question: Why did Samir walk home slowly?
options: He didn't want to arrive at an empty flat.
He was waiting for his friends.
questions.explanation: His parents were not home until seven, and he didn't want to arrive at the empty flat.

questions.question: How did Mr Abramov teach chess?
options: He explained that every piece had a job and asked "Why?" when Samir moved without thinking.
He let Samir win to make him happy.
He gave him books to read at home.
questions.explanation: He explained chess like a machine and asked "Why?" until Samir had a real answer.

questions.question: How did chess help Samir at school?
options: He joined the school chess team.
He started to look at maths problems in a new way.
questions.explanation: He looked at maths problems like the board, and his marks improved.

questions.question: What does Mr Abramov's final sentence mean?
options: Samir is now the best player in the city.
Samir has learnt enough to play against stronger people and keep learning.
Mr Abramov is angry that he lost.
questions.explanation: He means Samir is now good enough to play better players, even if he loses to them.
